title: Titulino Level Assessment Question Bank v2.0
description: One bank per TARGET language (en.json, es.json, pt.json) — never per language pair. The assessed material must be identical for every base language, or CEFR levels are not comparable between learners. CONVENTIONS FOR ANYONE ADDING CONTENT: (1) `stem` and `options` are target-language content and are NEVER translated. (2) Everything the learner reads in their own language — instructions, writing prompts, band labels, can-do text, phoneme hints — lives in the app i18n bundles (es_US.json / en_US.json / pt_BR.json) and is referenced here only by key. (3) ID format is {lang}-{band}-{nn} for questions and {lang}-{band}-p{nn} for pronunciation items, lowercase, two-digit zero-padded; e.g. en-b1-03, en-b1-p01. No 'assessment-' prefix: these ids appear only in assessment tables and never collide with the course namespace (supermarket-ch1-001). (4) Every band must hold 5 questions covering 5 DISTINCT `concept` values — the engine draws 2 of 5 at random, so duplicate concepts within a band can leave a band measuring only one grammar point. (5) Locale variants are enforced: en-US General American, pt-BR Brazilian, es-419 Latin American. No vosotros, no European Portuguese, no British spelling. IPA follows the same variants — critically, Spanish is seseo, so the phoneme θ must never appear in es.json.

schemaVersion.description: Loaders must validate this and fail loudly on mismatch rather than silently misreading a bank.

targetLanguage.description: The language being assessed. Matches the filename.

targetLocale.description: Content variant. es-419 is the metadata tag for Latin American Spanish; Azure speech uses es-MX for the same variant — both are correct in their own context, do not 'fix' one to match the other.

startBand.description: Always A2. Never derived from enrollment level — enrollment level is self-reported and unreliable, and a varying entry point would make results non-comparable.

writingPromptKey.description: i18n key, NOT literal text — the prompt is written in the learner's base language and injects the target language as a {targetLanguage} parameter. MUST be null on A1 and A2: those learners cannot produce usable written output.

instructionKey.description: Six keys only. The instruction says what ACTION the learner performs; anything more specific ('choose the present subjunctive for a wish') is concept detail and belongs in `concept`, not here.

stem.description: Target language, never translated. null only for chooseCorrectSentence, where the options are complete sentences and there is nothing to prompt with.

options.description: Target language, never translated. Distractors should be diagnostic — each wrong option ideally corresponds to a known error for the audience, not random noise.

correct.description: Must match one entry in options exactly.

concept.description: Namespaced grammar point, used for deterministic weak-area feedback with no AI. Four families: verb.* syntax.* lexis.* form.*. The vocabulary is shared across languages but BAND PLACEMENT is per-language — the subjunctive is B1 in Spanish and Portuguese (everyday speech) but C1 in English (rare, formal).

itemId.description: e.g. en-b1-p01. Stable and opaque — do not derive meaning from it in code.

text.description: The word or phrase the learner says. Target language.

ipa.description: Locale-correct IPA. en-US General American: rhotic, ae in dance, schwa-r. es-419: SESEO — theta must never appear (cielo is 'sjelo); yeismo (llave is 'ʝaβe). pt-BR: palatalisation t/d to tʃ/dʒ before i (dia is 'dʒiɐ); coda l to w (Brasil is bɾa'ziw); nasal vowels; open/close e-ɛ and o-ɔ.

focusPhoneme.description: The sound this item is chosen to drill. Must appear in phonemes[]. Not rendered by PhonemeDrawer today — carried as authoring metadata so weak-phoneme aggregation is possible later.

phonemes.description: Symbols only, in order. Multi-character units stay whole (tʃ, dʒ, eɪ, oʊ, nasal diphthongs). Hint TEXT is not stored here: a hint depends on both the target phoneme and the learner's base language, so the UI resolves assessment.phoneme.hint.{target}.{symbol} from i18n. Phonemes that transfer cleanly from the base language take no hint at all.
